title: Standard fppf coverings descend through affine inverse limits
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of affine $S$-schemes, and $T=\varprojlim_iT_i$. A standard fppf covering of an affine scheme $B$ is a finite family $\{V_a\to B\}_{a=1}^m$ of affine schemes, each flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], whose images cover $B$; maps between affine schemes are affine, so these maps are also quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence finitely presented. The case $m=0$ is allowed exactly when $B$ is empty. Every standard fppf covering $\{V_a\to T\}_{a=1}^m$ is isomorphic, as a family over $T$, to the base change of a standard fppf covering $\{V_{i,a}\to T_i\}_{a=1}^m$ for some $i\in I$.

source.place: Tag 049N (lemma-limit-fppf-topology), clause (1), tau=fppf; standard coverings as in Tag 021Q (definition-standard-fppf).

proof.text: Every $T_i$ is affine, so the transitions are affine morphisms by the affine-cover criterion (the one-element cover of the affine target has affine preimage), and the limit $T$ exists and is affine, being the spectrum of the colimit of the coordinate rings, by the limit lemma for affine transitions. Hence $T_i$, $T$ and $V_a$ are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. By the same criterion each $V_a\to T$ is affine, so quasi-compact and quasi-separated; together with its assumed local finite presentation this is finite presentation. These verify the hypotheses for finite-presentation descent. All changes of stage below use the canonical iterated-fibre-product identifications, which follow by cartesian-square pasting.

source.place: Tag 049N proof, first paragraph; Tag 01ZM hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply simultaneous finite-family finite-presentation descent to $(V_a\to T)_{a=1}^m$. Obtain $i_0\in I$, finitely presented morphisms $g_{0,a}:X_{0,a}\to T_{i_0}$ with qcqs sources, and isomorphisms $X_{0,a}\times_{T_{i_0}}T\cong V_a$ over $T$. For $j\ge i_0$ write $g_{j,a}:X_{j,a}\to T_j$ for the base changes. These remain finitely presented with qcqs sources. The identity of $T_{i_0}$ is also of finite presentation (on each affine chart it has the presentation with no generators or relations).

source.place: Tag 049N proof, first sentence; Tag 01ZM(1) and finite common refinement.

proof.text: For each $a$, apply affineness descent to $g_{0,a}$: its limit base change is $V_a\to T$, which is affine. Apply flatness descent to the same $g_{0,a}$: it is locally of finite presentation and its limit base change is the given flat map. The base, source and target at $i_0$ are qcqs, as required by both lemmas. Choose $i_1\ge i_0$ dominating the finitely many affine and flat stages. Affineness and flatness persist under base change, so every $g_{i_1,a}$ is affine and flat. Its source is affine because $T_{i_1}$ is affine, and its finite presentation persists. If $m=0$, choose $i_1=i_0$; there are no conditions to impose.

source.place: Tag 049N proof, second sentence; Tags 01ZN and 04AI.

proof.text: Apply finite-family joint-surjectivity descent with base system $(T_i)$, fixed stage $i_1$, finite index set $\{1,\ldots,m\}$, sources $U_a=X_{i_1,a}$, target $V=T_{i_1}$, and arrows $g_{i_1,a}$. Sources and target are finitely presented over $T_{i_1}$, and each arrow is locally of finite presentation. Their limit pullbacks identify with the original covering maps, so they are jointly surjective on points. Obtain $i_2\ge i_1$ at which the family is jointly surjective. The cited statement allows the empty index set: when $m=0$ its conclusion says that $T_{i_2}$ has no points, exactly the required empty covering case.

source.place: Tag 049N proof, remaining joint-surjectivity assertion; Tag 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective), finite-family formulation.

proof.text: Set $V_{i_2,a}=X_{i_1,a}\times_{T_{i_1}}T_{i_2}$. Base change preserves affineness, flatness and finite presentation, and an affine morphism to affine $T_{i_2}$ has affine source. Step 4 gives joint surjectivity, so these maps form a standard fppf covering. Cartesian-square pasting identifies $V_{i_2,a}\times_{T_{i_2}}T$ with $X_{0,a}\times_{T_{i_0}}T$; composing with the chosen isomorphisms gives $V_a$ over $T$, for every original label $a$. All structure maps to $S$ are obtained by composing with $T_{i_2}\to S$ and the isomorphisms over $T$ automatically respect them.

proof_origin.place: Tag 049N(1), fppf case, using Tags 01ZM, 01ZN, 04AI; joint-surjectivity substep via the existing finite-family form of Tag 07RR.
